clue.text: One twice intervenes in tricky subject once concerning old Catholic

indicators.note: something tricky is twisty and awkward, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged
to intervene is to come between, so the single letters go inside the rearranged word

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
one is the Roman numeral I, used twice

explanation.surface: Someone keeps butting in on an awkward topic that once concerned an old Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: The two I's go in separately: JEBUS-I-T-I-C. 'Once' marks the word as obsolete: a Jebusite was a 17th-century nickname for a Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: Jebusite was a hostile historical label for a Roman Catholic, and the adjective describes anything relating to such people.

explanation.definitionFit: Earst is an archaic adverb meaning formerly or at first, a variant of erst found in Spenser.
